# Real-time laboratory report: latency distributions and deadline suitability

**Platform:** Radxa Dragon Q6A (QCS6490), Hexagon v68 CDSP + Cortex-A78
**Measurement date:** 2026-11-14 UTC
**Raw data:** `results/rt-2026-11-14/raw/`
**Machine summary:** `results/rt-2026-11-14/summary.md` (generated by `tools/rt_analyze.cpp`)
**Detailed Russian record:** [`rt-report.ru.md`](rt-report.ru.md)

## Verdict

| Variant (idle condition) | 100 µs | 50 µs | 20 µs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CPU A78, pinned | suitable | suitable | suitable |
| DSP compute-only | suitable | suitable | suitable |
| DSP + one FastRPC `step` | not suitable | not suitable | not suitable |
| DSP + FastRPC `step`, memory load | not suitable | not suitable | not suitable |

“Suitable” is an empirical p99.9/observed-max criterion, not a WCET guarantee.
The complete table for all conditions is in `results/rt-2026-11-14/summary.md`
and the detailed report.

## 1. Question and pre-registered criteria

The question is not only the median FOC step time, but the distribution, the
tail, and fitness for 100 µs (10 kHz), 50 µs (20 kHz) and 20 µs (50 kHz)
control periods.

Criteria fixed before the runs:

- **suitable:** p99.9 < period and observed maximum < period;
- **conditional:** p99.9 < period but observed maximum ≥ period;
- **not suitable:** p99.9 ≥ period.

The observed maximum is not a WCET estimate and is not a guarantee.

## 2. Setup and interference control

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Board | Radxa Dragon Q6A, QCS6490 |
| Kernel | Linux 6.18.2-3-qcom, aarch64 |
| CPU | 8 cores: A55 0–3, A78 4–6, A78 prime 7 |
| Measured core | CPU 7, `taskset -c 7` |
| Governor | `performance`; `scaling_cur_freq` = 2,707,200 kHz |
| IRQ affinity | 97 IRQs moved off CPU 7; 41 could not be changed; `default_smp_affinity=7f` |
| `isolcpus` | absent from `/proc/cmdline`; cannot be changed without reboot |
| CDSP | Hexagon v68, SDK 6.4.0.2, tools 19.0.04 |
| CDSP clock | 1.170 GHz direct probe; 1.1572 GHz indirect estimate |
| Temperature | 58.3–90.7 °C across zones; no separate throttling control |

The governor and IRQ settings are not persistent across reboot and were applied
before each run. The helper is `scripts/irq_off.sh`.

## 3. Method

- **DSP samples:** `sampler_run(batch_steps, sample_count, ...)` executes
  `sample_count` batches of 16 steps and stores per-batch cycles in a static
  `uint16_t[100000]` array on the DSP. The host retrieves it with scalar
  `sampler_get(idx)` calls, preserving the scalar-argument contract.
- **Host samples:** `rt-step` times each RPC `step` with
  `clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW)`; `rt-cpu` times a 16-step CPU batch;
  `rt-bench` times a `bench(..., iterations=16)` RPC.
- **Warm-up:** the first 100 samples of each file are marked `warmup=1` and
  excluded. The DSP+RPC step series was repeated with `warmup=1000` after drift
  was found; its N is 102,000 versus 101,700 for the other variants.
- **Sample count:** 34,000 × 3 interleaved rounds per configuration (101,700
  accepted); the `bench` series has 10.5k × 10 chunks (104,000 accepted).
- **Interleaving:** each round runs CPU → DSP compute → DSP+RPC step, then the
  next round, reducing the risk of assigning thermal drift to one variant.
- **Conditions:** `idle`; `cpu-load` (2 workers on CPU 4–5); `memory-load`
  (2 read/write threads, 256 MiB each, CPU 4–5); `dsp-load` (background DSP
  `bench`, CPU measured).

Timer-read cost was measured separately and subtracted: CPU
`clock_gettime` 40.143 ns/call (two calls per batch, 5.018 ns/step at batch
16); DSP `qurt_get_core_pcycles` 24.015 cycles/call (48.03 cycles per batch,
3.00 cycles/step). Raw CSV files are uncorrected; the analyzer applies the
correction.

## 4. Distributions (ns per step, timer overhead removed)

| Condition | Variant | n | p50 | p99 | p99.9 | Observed max |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| idle | CPU A78 scalar | 101,700 | 56.9 | 66.6 | 310.7 | 1,886.2 |
| idle | DSP compute only | 101,700 | 330.2 | 352.8 | 366.5 | 394.7 |
| idle | DSP + FastRPC `step` | 102,000 | 71,534.7 | 361,588.3 | 1,045,649.9 | 7,794,085.7 |
| idle | DSP + FastRPC `bench` (16 steps/call) | 104,000 | 5,115.4 | 24,353.8 | 132,036.1 | 522,136.9 |
| cpu-load | CPU A78 scalar | 101,700 | 56.9 | 66.6 | 255.4 | 181,238.5 |
| cpu-load | DSP compute only | 101,700 | 330.2 | 352.8 | 367.2 | 392.3 |
| cpu-load | DSP + FastRPC `step` | 102,000 | 71,950.7 | 459,295.2 | 610,963.2 | 7,302,679.7 |
| memory-load | CPU A78 scalar | 101,700 | 56.9 | 69.9 | 393.1 | 5,200.0 |
| memory-load | DSP compute only | 101,700 | 330.2 | 352.8 | 367.4 | 430.9 |
| memory-load | DSP + FastRPC `step` | 102,000 | 122,263.7 | 1,220,440.7 | 1,453,878.7 | 27,258,721.7 |

The key result is the RPC tail: even at idle, one `step` RPC has a p99.9 of
about **1.05 ms** and an observed maximum of **7.79 ms**. A 16-step `bench`
call amortizes the RPC and is much better, but it is a different execution model
from one control update per RPC.

## 5. Deadline suitability

| Condition | Variant | 100 µs | 50 µs | 20 µs |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| idle | CPU A78 | suitable | suitable | suitable |
| idle | DSP compute-only | suitable | suitable | suitable |
| idle | DSP + RPC step | not suitable (2.29% > 100 µs) | not suitable | not suitable |
| cpu-load | CPU A78 | conditional | conditional | conditional |
| cpu-load | DSP compute-only | suitable | suitable | suitable |
| cpu-load | DSP + RPC step | not suitable | not suitable | not suitable |
| memory-load | CPU A78 | suitable | suitable | suitable |
| memory-load | DSP compute-only | suitable | suitable | suitable |
| memory-load | DSP + RPC step | not suitable | not suitable | not suitable |

Under CPU load the CPU still meets each period at p99.9, but a small number of
samples exceed it; the observed maximum is therefore above the period. That is
reported as conditional, not as a guarantee.

## 6. Effect size

Bootstrap medians (1,000 draws, 95% interval) for idle:

| Comparison | Median ratio | Median difference | p99 difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DSP compute / CPU | 5.807 [5.806, 5.810] | +273.3 ns | +286.2 ns |
| DSP+RPC step / CPU | 1,258.1 [1,258.1, 1,259.0] | +71,477.9 ns | +361,521.7 ns |
| DSP+RPC step / DSP compute | 216.65 [216.58, 216.70] | +71,204.5 ns | +361,235.5 ns |

Memory load amplifies the RPC tail: DSP+RPC step / CPU reaches 2,150× by median
and the p99 difference exceeds 1.2 ms.

## 7. DSP cycles (primary metric)

| Condition | n | p50 | p99 | p99.9 | Observed max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| idle | 101,700 | 386.31 | 412.75 | 428.81 | 461.81 |
| cpu-load | 101,700 | 386.31 | 412.75 | 429.64 | 458.94 |
| memory-load | 101,700 | 386.31 | 412.75 | 429.89 | 504.12 |

DSP compute is stable across load conditions; the large ns/step changes in the
RPC variants are transport and scheduling effects, not additional DSP work.

## 8. Limitations

- “Suitable” is empirical, not a WCET proof; the observed maximum is not a
  guaranteed bound.
- The governor and IRQ affinity are reapplied manually and are not persistent
  across reboot.
- `isolcpus` is absent; CPU 7 shares the kernel scheduler with other work.
- No separate throttling control; zone temperatures reached 90.7 °C.
- The DSP+RPC `step` variant is one RPC per control step. The 16-step `bench`
  variant is reported for contrast and is not the same real-time model.
- Raw CSVs are retained; the summary is reproducible with `tools/rt_analyze.cpp`.

## 9. Reproduction

```bash
scripts/run_rt_suite.sh results/rt-2026-11-14
scripts/run_rt_bench_suite.sh results/rt-2026-11-14
./build/rt/rt_analyze --input results/rt-2026-11-14 --output results/rt-2026-11-14
```

The build directory is generated and not committed. See
`results/rt-2026-11-14/SHA256SUMS` and `summary.md` for the retained evidence.
